customer_question: We wrote 'none' for the Host Stack QDID/DN field on the quote request form since we don't use it -- is that the right way to answer, and what do you need to know to quote this?
question_variants: What does it mean if we say 'none' for Host Stack QDID/DN?
Does our product even have a Host layer, or do we just not have it registered yet?
Why do you need to know more about what 'none' means before quoting?
actual_issue: A customer answered 'none' to the Bluetooth quote-request form's field asking for the Host Stack's QDID/DN, but this answer was ambiguous between two materially different scenarios: the product not implementing a Host layer at all, versus the product implementing a Host layer that simply isn't yet registered (and therefore has no QDID/DN) -- a distinction that significantly affects the scope of testing and registration needed.
plain_english_explanation: On a Bluetooth quote-request form, being asked for an existing registration ID for a particular layer of the product (like the Host software layer) and answering 'none' could mean two very different things: either that layer genuinely doesn't exist in the product, or that it does exist but just hasn't been certified yet. Those two situations require completely different amounts of testing and registration work, so a vague 'none' answer needs to be pinned down before a quote can be accurately prepared.
consultant_answer: The submitted Bluetooth quote-request form was missing required items needed to quote accurately: (1) how the Declaration Fee (registration fee) would be paid -- either the applicant wiring directly to Bluetooth SIG, or requesting Allion to act as USD wire-transfer agent (the customer chose the latter and asked for a quote covering that service); and (2) the Host Stack's QDID/DN and implemented profiles, which is mandatory to fill in, with 'none' acceptable only for profile items that are genuinely not implemented. When the customer wrote 'none' for the Host Stack QDID/DN itself, the consultant asked for clarification on which of two distinct situations this represented: (a) this product does not implement a Host layer at all, or (b) this product does implement a Host layer, but it does not yet have a QDID/DN because that layer has not been certified.
decision_logic: A 'none' or blank answer to a quote-request field asking for an existing QDID/DN of a specific subsystem (such as the Host Stack) is not informative enough to scope a quote on its own, since it could mean either that the subsystem doesn't exist in the product or that it exists but is simply unregistered -- the latter implies a real, billable scope of testing and registration work that the former does not, so this distinction must be clarified with the customer before finalizing the quote.
final_recommendation: When a customer answers 'none' to a quote-request field asking for an existing QDID/DN for a given subsystem, ask them to clarify whether that subsystem is genuinely not implemented in the product, or whether it is implemented but simply not yet registered, before finalizing the quote's scope.
risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming 'none' means the Host layer doesn't exist, when it actually exists but is unregistered, would understate the true scope of testing and registration work in the quote, risking a significant cost and schedule gap discovered only after the engagement is underway.
